evidence: Ter. Ad. 329: Satin' hoc certum est? — Certum.
Cic. Att. 2.19.5: certī sumus perīsse omnia
terms.comment: Of a thing, certum est, it is certain; of a person, certus sum with an accusative and infinitive, I am sure that (Cicero, of bad news). But certum est mihi with an infinitive is “I have decided” (see decide), and certior fierī is “be told, be informed”.

terms.gloss: I’m sure, I know for certain
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: the adverb certō is found only in comedy and in Cicero, most often in his letters; certē, certainly, belongs to every period.

terms.gloss: take as certain, be sure of

terms.grammar: phrase: imperative of faciō, with the subjunctive
terms.comment: Also cūrā ut, as in Cicero’s sign-off cūrā ut valeās.

phrases.latin: Satin' hoc certum est? — Certum: hīsce oculīs egomet vīdī.
phrases.english: Is that quite certain? — Certain: I saw it with these very eyes.
A citizen? — I think so; we don’t know for sure.

phrases.latin: tē quandō exspectēmus fac ut sciam
phrases.english: make sure you let me know when to expect you
